dissents: Judge A: Behavioral changes (CRLF normalization, schema validation accepting null) violate the port contract — a port should preserve the original's semantics; Judge B: These might be intentional robustness improvements, but treating them as transparent additions misleads about the scope of change
Judge A: The evidence pointer (1-12 vs actual 4-line wrapper) indicates insufficient review of delivered artifacts; Judge B: This is a reporting accuracy issue separate from code correctness
extras: CRLF-to-LF normalization for text files before sha256 computation — changes artifact verification behavior beyond the original shell script
Text file detection via extension patterns and null-byte scanning

refuted_misses: The Node port does not preserve raw sha256 semantics from the original shell script: it normalizes CRLF for text files before hashing artifact_paths and moved-file candidates, so it can accept/reject checksums differently from sha256sum and does not strictly verify the file bytes it claims to verify.
The node report's evidence pointer scripts/check-node-report.sh:1-12 is invalid/stale because the delivered wrapper is only 4 lines long.
survived_misses: The Node schema validation is not a faithful port of the original check-node-report.sh because it allows verdict: null, while the original required verdict to be a non-empty string.
